S2 T2 Verified -1 ROOT-CAUSED (not retried) and fixed; re-pushed as patch set 2 of Gerrit 1896 with Change-Id preserved. Two jobs failed with ONE root cause: a COMMENT-HYGIENE gate rejected a raw commit SHA in a source comment - my test docstring said 'Verified against the pre-extraction code at 4758d47f82'. The gate's message is that source comments carry CURRENT state while the ticket system owns history, so a resolvable ticket/epic/story id is required instead of a SHA. Replaced with the ticket citation (RP-02 S1, vivacious-widish-indianabat). scripts/check_comment_hygiene.py now exit 0, and its in-process mirror tests/unit/test_comment_hygiene_guard.py::test_the_real_tree_is_clean passes; the pytest job's only failure was that same mirror (1 failed, 14167 passed), so both jobs collapse to the single cause.
TWO PROCESS LESSONS worth carrying for S3. (1) make lint does NOT cover every Verified gate. The failing gate ran as a separate CI step, and I had verified make lint, make typecheck, config-ownership, config-reads and the env registry but never scripts/check_comment_hygiene.py. Other CI-only steps I have now seen in that job: make config-check, scripts/check_verify_gate_parity.py, check_dco_identity.py, check_criteria_vocabulary.py, check_skill_frontmatter.py, zizmor and actionlint. (2) my regression run was scoped to tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/ and tests/interfaces/store/, which MISSED tests/unit/test_comment_hygiene_guard.py - a repo-wide guard living outside the subsystem tree. For S3 I will run the guard tests plus the whole tests/unit/ tree, or at minimum add check_comment_hygiene.py and the guard test to the pre-push checklist. Also worth noting: no source comment in RP-02 may cite a commit SHA, which matters because this epic's whole method is characterizing pre-extraction behavior - the citation must be the TICKET, not the commit.
Filed captious-hennish-mangabey (02c4-4e64-5ee3-459c) discovered_from sportive-statued-goose: the integration idempotency oracle at test_reconcile_idempotency.py:311 patches binding_store_mod._now_iso, but clear_absent now resolves it from binding_lifecycle, so that patch no longer reaches it. The test still passes and the contract is covered directly by my held-out clear_absent no-dirty test, so coverage moved tiers rather than vanishing - but the integration oracle's blast radius narrowed and the ticket requires proving the widened patch goes RED under a seeded unconditional-stamp mutation.
